bullets.title: Orchestrated Incident
bullets.creator: Gramatik
bullets.note: ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KK2zeLbKlnc), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/track/3ktye8UiJXiXHbp1Elonn6?si=913e6b689e20428d)) by [Gramatik](https://www.gramatik.net/). I wrote a good portion of [_The 4-Hour Chef_](https://www.amazon.com/4-Hour-Chef-Cooking-Learning-Anything/dp/1328519163/) (in fact, a book on accelerated learning) to this track on repeat. It’s not everyone’s cup of tea, but I find the upbeat instrumentals fantastic for writing flow. I have a lot of [Gramatik](https://www.gramatik.net/) and [Beats Antique](https://www.beatsantique.com/)—try “[Circulation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jQmXRKaPbRU)”—in my playlist for writing sessions.

bullets.section: What I’m wearing for long hikes
bullets.title: L’eggs Women’s Everyday Knee Highs
bullets.note: OK, OK, hear me out. An old Italian fella, veteran of the Camino de Santiago, shared this gem with a close friend of mine: Skip fancy sock liners and just put these on before your hiking socks. _Et voilà!_ No blisters. So far, it’s worked like a charm.

bullets.title: Travels with Charley: In Search of America
bullets.creator: John Steinbeck
bullets.note: . This was originally given to me by my dear mom, who knows I’ve fantasized for ages about a countrywide road trip with my pooch, [Molly](https://www.instagram.com/p/CgmvolcA5ar/). The book was published in 1962, the same year Steinbeck won the Nobel Prize in Literature for his work. It’s beautiful and surprisingly hilarious at points. Here is a brief description: “With Charley, his French poodle, Steinbeck drives the interstates and the country roads, dines with truckers, encounters bears at Yellowstone and old friends in San Francisco. Along the way, he reflects on the American character, racial hostility, the particular form of American loneliness he finds almost everywhere, and the unexpected kindness of strangers.”

links.catalog_title: Travels with Charley in Search of America

bullets.title: The Price of Everything
bullets.note: ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iejpS_PpPJk), [Apple TV](https://tv.apple.com/us/movie/the-price-of-everything/umc.cmc.7ij92u1chb9mcl0hww0foiwug)), directed by [Nathaniel Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathaniel_Kahn). I originally watched this film after both my brother and a close friend raved about it, and I was prompted to rewatch it after [Kevin Rose brought it up](https://tim.blog/2022/09/23/a-rare-in-person-random-show-kevin-rose/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf) in [the most recent Random Show episode](https://tim.blog/2022/09/23/a-rare-in-person-random-show-kevin-rose/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf). It is often funny, sometimes nauseating, and always entertaining. Here’s the description: “With unprecedented access to pivotal artists and the white-hot market surrounding them, _The Price of Everything_ dives deep into the contemporary art world, holding a mirror up to our values and our times—where everything can be bought and sold.”
